1.dye_uM: Nominal thymol blue concentration in the prepared standard, in µM.
1.readout: R is A545/A485, and R* is (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750), using absorbance at the indicated wavelengths in nm.
1.plate_n: Number of distinct physical microplates contributing at least one eligible standard mean to the fit.
1.plate_mean_n: Number of four-well standard means on individual microplates with both a finite ratio and a measured pH.
1.level_n: Number of distinct measured pH values among the standard means used to fit the curve.
1.fit_rmse: Root mean squared difference between the observed standard means and the fitted ratios, in ratio units.
1.r_squared: Fraction of the variation in the observed standard means explained by the fitted curve.
1.identified: True when all four fitted parameters pass the numerical identification checks, including parameter precision and coverage of the midpoint by the measured pH values.
1.converged: True when the numerical optimizer reported a solution for the four-parameter logistic fit.
1.identification_flags: Diagnostic reasons for an unavailable or weakly determined fit, such as too few finite levels or a poorly determined parameter. A blank means no diagnostic flag was raised.
1.ci_df: Degrees of freedom for 95% Student t intervals using HC3 uncertainty clustered by physical plate, equal to the contributing plate count minus one (−1 indicates no contributing plates).
1.bottom: Fitted lower asymptote of the indicator ratio.
1.bottom_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the lower asymptote (ratio units).
1.bottom_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the lower asymptote (ratio units).
1.span: Fitted upper asymptote minus the lower asymptote, in ratio units.
1.span_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the fitted ratio span (ratio units).
1.span_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the fitted ratio span (ratio units).
1.midpoint: Measured pH at which the fitted ratio is halfway between the two asymptotes.
1.midpoint_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the half-response pH.
1.midpoint_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the half-response pH.
1.slope: Steepness coefficient of the base-10 logistic curve, per pH unit, with positive values indicating a ratio that falls as pH increases.
1.slope_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the base-10 logistic steepness (per pH unit).
1.slope_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the base-10 logistic steepness (per pH unit).
1.unavailable_plate_mean_n: Number of scheduled plate-by-standard means without an eligible four-well ratio mean.

2.metric: Within-plate quantity selected from the range of standard means, the pooled within-standard well SD, or the range divided by that SD.
2.raw_mean: Arithmetic mean of the plate-specific metric calculated with the measured absorbance ratio A545/A485.
2.corrected_mean: Arithmetic mean of the plate-specific metric after A750 is subtracted from both A545 and A485 before forming the ratio.
2.plate_n: Number of physical plates with a finite log₂ ratio of the corrected metric to the measured metric.
2.estimate: Mean across plates of log₂(corrected metric/measured metric), where zero denotes equal metrics.
2.sd: Sample standard deviation among the plate-specific log₂(corrected/measured) values.
2.ci_low: Lower limit of the 95% Student t confidence interval for the mean plate log₂ ratio.
2.ci_high: Upper limit of the 95% Student t confidence interval for the mean plate log₂ ratio.
2.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided one-sample t-test p-value for a mean plate log₂ ratio of zero.
2.p_holm: P-value after Holm adjustment across the tests of span, pooled within-standard SD and their quotient.
2.multiplicity_family_n: Number of estimable metric tests included in the Holm adjustment.
2.status: Indicates whether the mean log₂ ratio and its interval could be estimated from the contributing physical plates.
2.geometric_ratio: Geometric mean of the plate-specific corrected/measured ratios, equal to 2 raised to the mean log₂ ratio.
2.ratio_ci_low: Lower 95% confidence limit for the corrected/measured fold change, obtained by exponentiating the lower log₂ limit with base 2.
2.ratio_ci_high: Upper 95% confidence limit for the corrected/measured fold change, obtained by exponentiating the upper log₂ limit with base 2.

3.acid_M: Nominal H₂SO₄ concentration (M) of the ferric mixture that defines the comparison, including the matching pH range used for the held-out acid standards.
3.matrix: Prediction target, either acid standards on the microplate withheld from calibration or ferric mixtures evaluated with the acid calibration.
3.readout_or_comparison: Measured A545/A485 (R), its A750-corrected counterpart (R*), or the paired comparison of these two readouts for the same plate and standard.
3.metric: Bias is predicted minus reference pH, RMSE is root mean squared prediction error, and technical SD is well-to-well ratio scatter converted to pH by the local calibration slope.
3.unit: pH units for errors, SDs and paired differences, or a dimensionless fold for the paired corrected/measured SD ratio.
3.attempted_n: All physical plate–standard observations considered before pH-range filtering for a single readout, or observations within the shared pH support of both readouts for a paired comparison.
3.eligible_n: Physical plate–standard observations on shared pH support with a finite prediction for the selected readout, or finite predictions for both readouts in paired comparisons.
3.support_reference_pH_min: Lowest measured reference pH retained within the common bins for the row’s readout or readout pair, before requiring a finite inverse prediction.
3.support_reference_pH_max: Highest measured reference pH retained within the common bins for the row’s readout or readout pair, before requiring a finite inverse prediction.
3.support_shared_bin_n: Number of occupied 0.25-pH-unit reference bins shared by the acid standards and ferric mixtures for this readout or pair.
3.estimate: Metric computed with equal weight per shared pH bin, with paired rows giving corrected minus measured bias or RMSE, or corrected divided by measured technical SD.
3.ci_low: Lower 95% bootstrap confidence limit (2.5th percentile) from resampling whole wells within each plate and standard and refitting the calibration.
3.ci_high: Upper 95% bootstrap confidence limit (97.5th percentile) from resampling whole wells within each plate and standard and refitting the calibration.
3.bootstrap_requested_n: Number of whole-well bootstrap resamples requested for this metric.
3.bootstrap_success_n: Number of resamples yielding a finite value of this metric, with limits reported only when at least 20 and at least 80% of requested resamples succeed.

4.acid_M: Nominal H₂SO₄ concentration in the dye-free ferric calibration series, in M.
4.plate_n: Number of distinct physical microplates contributing at least one eligible standard mean at this acid concentration.
4.plate_mean_n: Number of plate-by-standard mean A380 values paired with a measured, nonnegative total Fe concentration for the fit.
4.level_n: Number of distinct measured total Fe concentrations represented among the fitted standard means.
4.fit_rmse: Root mean squared difference between observed and fitted A380 values, in absorbance units (AU).
4.r_squared: Fraction of variation in the observed standard means explained by the fitted ferric response.
4.identified: True when all four fitted parameters pass the numerical identification checks, including parameter precision and coverage of the half-response concentration.
4.converged: True when the numerical optimizer reported a solution for the stretched-exponential ferric response model.
4.identification_flags: Diagnostic reasons for an unavailable or weakly determined fit, with a blank indicating that no flag was raised.
4.ci_df: Degrees of freedom for 95% Student t intervals using HC3 uncertainty clustered by physical plate, equal to the contributing plate count minus one.
4.bottom: Fitted A380 at zero total Fe, in AU.
4.bottom_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the zero-Fe baseline (AU).
4.bottom_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the zero-Fe baseline (AU).
4.span: Fitted increase in A380 from the zero-Fe baseline to the upper plateau, in AU.
4.span_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the increase from baseline to plateau (AU).
4.span_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the increase from baseline to plateau (AU).
4.midpoint: Measured total Fe concentration (mM) at which the model reaches half the fitted increase above baseline.
4.midpoint_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the half-response total Fe concentration (mM).
4.midpoint_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the half-response total Fe concentration (mM).
4.slope: Dimensionless exponent controlling the shape of the stretched-exponential ferric response curve.
4.slope_ci_low: Lower 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the dimensionless ferric response exponent.
4.slope_ci_high: Upper 95% plate-clustered confidence limit for the dimensionless ferric response exponent.

5.series_ID: Chemical standard series, either ferric standards in 1 M H₂SO₄ or ferrous standards in 0.001 or 1 M H₂SO₄.
5.n: Number of reference levels used in the ordinary least-squares regression, each represented by a total Fe concentration and a mean of three Fe²⁺ titrations.
5.x_min_M: Lowest measured total Fe concentration included in the regression, in M.
5.x_max_M: Highest measured total Fe concentration included in the regression, in M.
5.slope: Fitted increase in Fe²⁺ measured by cerimetry per unit increase in measured total Fe (M/M).
5.slope_ci_low: Lower 95% Student t confidence limit for the regression slope (M/M), treating measured total Fe as fixed.
5.slope_ci_high: Upper 95% Student t confidence limit for the regression slope (M/M), treating measured total Fe as fixed.
5.intercept_M: Fitted Fe²⁺ concentration at zero total Fe, in M.
5.intercept_ci_low_M: Lower 95% Student t confidence limit for the fitted intercept, in M.
5.intercept_ci_high_M: Upper 95% Student t confidence limit for the fitted intercept, in M.
5.sy_x_M: Residual standard deviation of measured Fe²⁺ about the fitted line, in M.
5.residual_df: Residual degrees of freedom, equal to the number of fitted reference levels minus two for the estimated intercept and slope.
5.slope_vs_zero_p: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for the hypothesis that the slope equals zero.
5.slope_zero_p_holm: P-value for a zero slope after Holm adjustment across all estimable slope and intercept tests in the three series.
5.slope_vs_one_p: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for the hypothesis that the slope equals one (a 1 M/M response).
5.slope_one_p_holm: P-value for a unit slope after Holm adjustment across all estimable slope and intercept tests in the three series.
5.intercept_vs_zero_p: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for the hypothesis that the intercept equals 0 M Fe²⁺.
5.intercept_zero_p_holm: P-value for a zero intercept after Holm adjustment across all estimable slope and intercept tests in the three series.

6.readout: Absorbance at 380 nm (A380) or 428 nm (A428), or their within-plate difference A380 − A428.
6.ferric_plate_n: Number of physical microplates contributing a mean response for ferric standards.
6.ferrous_plate_n: Number of physical microplates contributing a mean response for ferrous standards.
6.common_level_n: Number of measured ferric reference concentrations with a finite response on every plate at both wavelengths after alignment of the ferrous series by interpolation.
6.reference_min_M: Lowest measured total Fe concentration on the common reference grid, in M.
6.reference_max_M: Highest measured total Fe concentration on the common reference grid, in M.
6.estimate: Mean ferric minus mean ferrous response (AU), giving equal weight to common concentrations within a plate and to plates within a chemical series.
6.ci_low: Lower 95% Welch t confidence limit for the ferric-minus-ferrous contrast, in AU.
6.ci_high: Upper 95% Welch t confidence limit for the ferric-minus-ferrous contrast, in AU.
6.welch_df: Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom for the confidence interval, calculated from the variance among plates and the plate count in each chemical series.

7.contrast: Direction of the subtraction at matched ferric-standard positions, either A750-corrected minus measured A380 or absorbance with dye minus absorbance without dye.
7.context: Dye condition held fixed for corrected-minus-measured contrasts, or readout held fixed for dyed-minus-undyed contrasts.
7.plate_n: Number of physical microplates with a finite paired absorbance difference.
7.estimate: Mean paired difference in absorbance units (AU), with standard-position differences averaged equally within each plate and plates weighted equally.
7.sd: Sample standard deviation of the paired absorbance difference across physical microplates, in AU.
7.ci_low: Lower limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean paired absorbance difference, in AU.
7.ci_high: Upper limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean paired absorbance difference, in AU.
7.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for a one-sample t test of whether the mean paired absorbance difference is zero.
7.p_holm: P-value after Holm adjustment across the four ferric-standard contrasts.
7.multiplicity_family_n: Number of contrasts with finite p-values in the Holm adjustment family (the four ferric-standard contrasts).
7.status: Whether the plate-level mean and its interval could be estimated. A single contributing plate permits a mean only.

8.assay: Identifies the thymol-blue absorbance ratio assay for pH or the ferric absorbance assay for iron.
8.dye: Nominal concentration of added thymol blue, in micromoles per liter (µM).
8.readout: The optical signal used in the calculation. R = A545/A485 and R* = (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750). A380 is absorbance at 380 nm and A*380 = A380 − A750.
8.paired_well_n: Total well pairs with eligible measurements of the same standard with and without the lid, summed across plates.
8.paired_level_n_min: Smallest number of matched standard levels contributing to a single physical plate’s lid contrast.
8.paired_level_n_max: Largest number of matched standard levels contributing to a single physical plate’s lid contrast.
8.plate_n: Number of physical microplates with a finite normalized lid contrast.
8.estimate: Mean across plates of 100 × (lid-present minus lid-absent response) / lid-absent response span. Within a plate, paired well differences are averaged within each standard, then equally across standards.
8.sd: Sample standard deviation of the normalized lid contrast across physical microplates, as a percentage of the lid-absent response span.
8.ci_low: Lower limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean normalized lid contrast, as a percentage of the lid-absent response span.
8.ci_high: Upper limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean normalized lid contrast, as a percentage of the lid-absent response span.
8.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for a one-sample t test of whether the mean normalized lid contrast is zero.
8.p_holm: P-value after Holm adjustment across the four lid contrasts.
8.multiplicity_family_n: Number of contrasts with finite p-values in the Holm adjustment family (the four lid contrasts).
8.status: Whether the plate-level mean and its interval could be estimated. A single contributing plate permits a mean only.

9.assay: Identifies the thymol-blue absorbance ratio assay for pH or the ferric absorbance assay for iron.
9.dye: Nominal concentration of added thymol blue, in micromoles per liter (µM).
9.readout: The optical signal used in the calculation. R = A545/A485 and R* = (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750). A380 is absorbance at 380 nm and A*380 = A380 − A750.
9.metric: Drift summary for each plate. Endpoint rows use final minus initial signal as a percentage of the initial span, or log₂(final/initial) for positive signals. Trajectory rows use the mean across post-initial acquisitions, the largest absolute acquisition mean, the largest absolute single-standard drift, or the root-mean-square drift across standard–acquisition pairs. Percentage drift uses the plate’s initial response span.
9.endpoint_day: Mean elapsed time in days from the initial acquisition to the final recorded acquisition across physical plates.
9.plate_n: Number of physical plates summarized for this assay, dye, and readout. In endpoint and common-support analyses, only plates with a finite value for the stated metric contribute to this count.
9.estimate: Arithmetic mean of the plate-level drift summaries, in log₂-fold units for log₂(final/initial) and percent of the initial response span for all other metrics.
9.sd: Sample standard deviation of the plate-level endpoint drift, in the units of the metric. Reported for the available-final-values rows.
9.interval_low: Lower 95% confidence limit for mean endpoint drift, or the smallest observed plate summary for descriptive trajectory metrics, as identified by interval_type.
9.interval_high: Upper 95% confidence limit for mean endpoint drift, or the largest observed plate summary for descriptive trajectory metrics, as identified by interval_type.
9.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided one-sample t-test p-value for zero mean endpoint drift, reported only for the available-final-values rows.
9.p_holm: P-value after Holm adjustment across the 12 available-final-values tests of signed change or log₂ fold change.
9.multiplicity_family_n: Number of endpoint tests with finite p-values in the Holm adjustment family. Blank for rows without a test.
9.status: Whether the support analysis estimated an endpoint mean with an interval or reported a descriptive summary. Blank where the source trajectory summary supplied no status.
9.support_basis: Standards and acquisitions entering the calculation. Available-final-values rows use the final acquisition. Available-level-and-acquisition rows use eligible post-initial measurements. In the sensitivity comparison, available_case uses each readout’s available levels at each acquisition and fixed_common_levels uses only levels valid for both readouts at every acquired index, including the initial read.
9.interval_type: Identifies a two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval across physical plates or the observed minimum-to-maximum range of plate summaries.
9.fixed_common_level_n: Total plate–standard combinations that met the fixed common-level rule, summed across plates. In the sensitivity analysis this count is reported for both available-case and fixed-support rows.

10.assay: Identifies the thymol-blue absorbance ratio assay for pH or the ferric absorbance assay for iron.
10.dye: Nominal concentration of added thymol blue, in micromoles per liter (µM).
10.readout: The optical signal used in the calculation. R = A545/A485 and R* = (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750). A380 is absorbance at 380 nm and A*380 = A380 − A750.
10.metric: Final-acquisition contrast or time-averaged contrast. The latter is the trapezoidal integral of the plate contrast divided by the observed duration, using actual acquisition times.
10.mean_endpoint_d: Mean elapsed time, in days, from the first to the last recorded storage acquisition across the physical plates.
10.maximum_absolute_observed_percent: Largest absolute concentration-matched plate contrast at any recorded acquisition on any plate, expressed as a percentage of that plate’s initial response span.
10.plate_n: Number of physical microplates with a finite edge-minus-interior drift contrast.
10.estimate: Mean across plates of the edge-well change from baseline minus the interior-well change from baseline, averaged over matched standards and scaled to percent of each plate’s initial response span. Positive values indicate greater signed drift at the edge.
10.sd: Sample standard deviation of the edge-minus-interior drift contrast across physical microplates, as a percentage of initial response span.
10.ci_low: Lower limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean edge-minus-interior drift contrast, as a percentage of initial response span.
10.ci_high: Upper limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean edge-minus-interior drift contrast, as a percentage of initial response span.
10.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for a one-sample t test of whether the mean edge-minus-interior drift contrast is zero.
10.p_holm: P-value after Holm adjustment across the 12 endpoint and time-average contrasts.
10.multiplicity_family_n: Number of contrasts with finite p-values in the Holm adjustment family (the 12 endpoint and time-average contrasts).
10.status: Whether the plate-level mean and its interval could be estimated. A single contributing plate permits a mean only.

11.medium: Growth-medium code for the standards. St-BS and St-YS denote Starkey medium with brown and yellow elemental sulfur, respectively.
11.readout: The optical signal used in the calculation. R = A545/A485 and R* = (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750). A380 is absorbance at 380 nm and A*380 = A380 − A750.
11.plate_n: Number of distinct physical microplates scheduled for the indicated medium and readout.
11.eligible_well_n: Total wells with an eligible value for this readout across the physical plates, including wells at levels with only one eligible measurement.
11.scheduled_well_n: Total wells assigned to the indicated medium and readout across the physical plates before eligibility filtering.
11.span_plate_n: Number of plates with at least two standard levels that each have two or more eligible well responses, permitting a response span.
11.span_mean: Arithmetic mean of the plate response spans. Each span is the highest minus the lowest replicated standard mean, in absorbance units for iron or ratio units for pH.
11.span_ci_low: Approximate lower 95% confidence limit for the arithmetic mean plate span, using a t interval on log(mean) with a delta-method standard error, then transforming back to the readout units.
11.span_ci_high: Approximate upper 95% confidence limit for the arithmetic mean plate span, calculated by the same log-scale method and expressed in the readout units.
11.sd_plate_n: Number of plates with an estimable pooled within-standard technical standard deviation for this readout.
11.technical_sd_mean: Arithmetic mean of the plate-level pooled technical standard deviations, in the readout units. Within each plate, well variances are pooled across replicated standards using their degrees of freedom.
11.sd_ci_low: Approximate lower 95% confidence limit for the arithmetic mean pooled technical standard deviation, using the log-scale delta-method t interval in the readout units.
11.sd_ci_high: Approximate upper 95% confidence limit for the arithmetic mean pooled technical standard deviation, using the log-scale delta-method t interval in the readout units.
11.span_sd_mean: Mean of the individual plates’ response span divided by pooled technical standard deviation, a dimensionless signal-to-scatter ratio.
11.median_rank_rho: Median plate-level Spearman rank correlation between reference value and standard mean response. Each correlation requires at least three replicated levels and variation in response.
11.plates_with_adjacent_reversal: Number of plates with at least one increase in mean pH-indicator response as reference pH rises, or a decrease in mean iron response as the iron reference rises, between adjacent scheduled standards with eligible means.

12.medium: Growth-medium code for the standards. St-BS and St-YS denote Starkey medium with brown and yellow elemental sulfur, respectively.
12.readout: Identifies the measured signal paired with its scatter-corrected counterpart. The pair is A380 and A380 − A750 for iron, or A545/A485 and (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750) for pH.
12.scheduled_plate_n: Number of physical plates assigned to this medium and measured-versus-corrected readout pair.
12.unavailable_plate_n: Number of scheduled plates without a finite log₂ ratio of corrected to measured Q. Both plate Q values must be finite and positive.
12.common_well_n: Total physical wells eligible for both readouts across scheduled plates, including plates where a Q contrast could not be estimated.
12.raw_Q_mean: Arithmetic mean of available plate Q values for the measured signal. For each plate, Q is the span of common-well standard means divided by pooled within-standard technical SD. Single-well means may contribute to span, while only replicated levels supply variance.
12.corrected_Q_mean: Arithmetic mean of available plate Q values for the scatter-corrected signal, calculated on the same eligible wells and using the same span and pooled-SD rules as the measured signal.
12.plate_n: Number of physical microplates with a finite log₂ Q contrast.
12.estimate: Mean across plates of log₂(corrected Q / measured Q). A positive value indicates greater response span relative to technical scatter after correction.
12.sd: Sample standard deviation of the log₂ Q contrast across physical microplates, in log₂-fold units.
12.ci_low: Lower limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean log₂ Q contrast, in log₂-fold units.
12.ci_high: Upper limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t confidence interval for the mean log₂ Q contrast, in log₂-fold units.
12.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for a one-sample t test of whether the mean log₂ Q contrast is zero.
12.p_holm: P-value after Holm adjustment across the seven estimable medium–readout contrasts.
12.multiplicity_family_n: Number of contrasts with finite p-values in the Holm adjustment family (the seven estimable medium–readout contrasts).
12.status: Whether the plate-level mean and its interval could be estimated. A single contributing plate permits a mean only.

13.metric: Outcome averaged within each starting batch, either the signed area under the response curve (AUC) to its first observed maximum or the elapsed time to that maximum.
13.comparison: AFM1 cohorts in numerator/denominator order. The number following plate or flask is the added Ga concentration in mM on a cation basis.
13.method: The two-sided test compares between-batch variances of log-transformed outcomes. It uses an independent-samples F test for plates versus flasks and a paired Pitman–Morgan test for two flask doses.
13.log_outcome_variance_ratio: Variance of the natural-log batch means in the numerator cohort divided by that in the denominator cohort. Values above 1 indicate greater dispersion in the numerator cohort.
13.ci_low: Lower unadjusted 95% confidence limit for the variance ratio, from the F distribution for independent batches or inversion of the Pitman–Morgan test for paired batches.
13.ci_high: Upper unadjusted 95% confidence limit for the same variance ratio.
13.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for the hypothesis that the two variances of log batch means are equal.
13.p_holm: P-value adjusted by Holm’s method within the independent-format or paired-flask comparison family.
13.status: Whether the variance comparison could be estimated, with the reason given when too few matched batches were available.
13.numerator_batch_n: Number of eligible starting batches in the numerator cohort, restricted to shared batches for paired flask comparisons.
13.denominator_batch_n: Number of eligible starting batches in the denominator cohort, restricted to shared batches for paired flask comparisons.
13.numerator_df: Numerator degrees of freedom for the independent F test, equal to the numerator batch count minus one.
13.denominator_df: Denominator degrees of freedom for the independent F test, equal to the denominator batch count minus one.
13.family_planned_n: Number of planned tests in the Holm adjustment, including unavailable comparisons. The adjustment covers two plate–flask tests or six paired flask-dose tests.
13.matched_batch_n: Number of starting batches with eligible outcomes under both flask doses in a paired comparison.
13.statistic: Signed t statistic for the paired Pitman–Morgan test. Positive values indicate greater log-outcome variance in the numerator cohort.
13.paired_test_df: Degrees of freedom for the Pitman–Morgan test, equal to the matched batch count minus two when at least three pairs are available.

14.metric: Outcome averaged within each starting batch, either the signed area under the response curve (AUC) to its first observed maximum or the elapsed time to that maximum.
14.cohort: Cultivation format and added Ga concentration in mM on a cation basis. Zero identifies no-additive AFM1 controls.
14.native_unit: Unit of the untransformed outcome, expressed in absorbance-unit days for plate AUC, mM days of apparent ferric iron for flask AUC, or days for elapsed time.
14.batch_n: Number of starting batches with a finite mean outcome for the cohort.
14.vessel_n: Number of distinct physical microplates or shake flasks recorded in the cohort’s batches.
14.native_mean: Arithmetic mean of the batch means in the native unit, weighting starting batches equally.
14.native_sd: Sample standard deviation of the batch means in the native unit.
14.cv_percent: Between-batch coefficient of variation, calculated as 100 times the sample standard deviation divided by the absolute value of the mean.
14.log_outcome_sd: Sample standard deviation of the natural logarithms of positive batch means.
14.centered_deviation_iqr_pp: Difference between the 75th and 25th percentiles of the batch deviations from the cohort mean, in percentage points. Each deviation is 100 × (batch mean/cohort mean − 1).
14.final_read_maximum_vessels: Number of physical vessels whose first observed maximum occurred at the final acquisition in at least one contributing trajectory.
14.status: Identifies the row as a descriptive summary of dispersion across starting batches.

15.comparison_quantity: Whether the effect is based on area under the curve (AUC) through the first observed maximum or on time to that maximum, each relative to the same-batch no-Ga control.
15.format: Whether the measurements were made in microplates or shake flasks.
15.readout: Identifies measured plate absorbance at 600 nm, same-well scatter-corrected absorbance (A600 − A750), or fluorescence-derived apparent flask OD600.
15.Ga_mM: Added gallium(III) sulfate concentration expressed as mM Ga³⁺, using the concentration calculated from the measured stock or the nominal concentration, as applicable.
15.unit: The effect and its uncertainty are expressed in percentage points for control-relative AUC or days for the timing difference.
15.candidate_batch_n: Number of starting batches represented at that dose and readout before requiring a finite estimate for the specified outcome.
15.batch_n: Number of starting batches with a finite estimate included in the mean effect.
15.physical_unit_n: Number of treated microplates or shake flasks with a finite control-relative estimate for the specified outcome.
15.effect: Mean of the starting-batch treatment effects. For AUC the vessel effect is 100 × (treated AUC/mean control AUC − 1). For timing it is treated time to maximum minus mean control time to maximum, in days.
15.between_batch_sd: Sample standard deviation of the starting-batch mean effects when at least two batches contribute, in the stated unit.
15.within_batch_unit_sd: Sample standard deviation across treated vessel effects when exactly one batch contributes and at least two vessel estimates are available, in the stated unit.
15.ci_low: Lower 95% Student’s t confidence limit for the mean effect across independent starting batches, calculated when at least three batches contribute.
15.ci_high: Upper 95% Student’s t confidence limit for the same mean effect, in the stated unit.
15.final_read_maximum_n: Number of treated vessel trajectories whose first observed maximum occurred at the final recorded acquisition, counted across candidate batches.
15.status: Indicates whether the batch count supports a confidence interval or only descriptive reporting.

16.citric_acid_mM: Final citric acid concentration in the microplate treatment, in mM.
16.Ga_mM: Final gallium(III) sulfate concentration expressed as mM Ga³⁺ in the microplate treatment.
16.paired_plate_n: Number of physical-plate endpoints with finite net absorbance changes measured at both wavelengths for the formulation.
16.batch_n: Number of distinct starting batches represented by the paired endpoints. Each contributes one mean difference.
16.net_380_mean_AU: Mean final net absorbance change at 380 nm (AU). The biotic change from baseline minus the matched abiotic change is averaged within each batch and then equally across batches.
16.net_428_mean_AU: Mean final net change at 428 nm (AU), using the same paired plates, abiotic correction and equal batch weighting.
16.paired_380_minus_428_AU: Mean within-plate difference in net change (380 minus 428 nm, AU), averaged within each batch and then equally across batches.
16.between_batch_difference_sd_AU: Sample standard deviation among starting-batch means of the paired wavelength difference, in AU.
16.ci_low: Lower unadjusted 95% Student’s t confidence limit for the mean paired wavelength difference across starting batches, in AU.
16.ci_high: Upper unadjusted 95% Student’s t confidence limit for the same difference, in AU.
16.statistic: One-sample t statistic testing whether the batch means of the paired 380-minus-428 nm differences average to zero.
16.df: Degrees of freedom of the t test, equal to the number of contributing starting batches minus one.
16.p_value: Unadjusted two-sided p-value for the test of zero mean paired wavelength difference.
16.p_holm: P-value adjusted by Holm’s method across the 18 citric acid–Ga formulations.
16.days_min: Shortest elapsed time in days to a contributing plate endpoint, using the 380 nm acquisition time.
16.days_max: Longest elapsed time in days to a contributing plate endpoint, using the 380 nm acquisition time.
16.status: Indicates whether at least three starting batches supplied paired differences for the exploratory t test.

17.comparison_quantity: Identifies mean AUC relative to each format’s no-additive control or mean elapsed time to the first observed maximum. Plate A380 and flask apparent Fe³⁺ generation are the underlying signals.
17.additive: Identifies the substance used for dose matching. Al, Cu, Ga and VO denote sulfate salts of those cations (VO is vanadyl). NaCl and citric acid identify those compounds.
17.plate_dose_mM: Reported concentration of the matched additive in the microplate, in mM on a cation basis for metal sulfates.
17.flask_dose_mM: Reported concentration of the matched additive in the shake flask, on the same mM basis as the plate dose.
17.Ga_mM: Additional Ga³⁺ concentration (mM) in a citric acid formulation. When Ga is the matched additive, its exposure is given by the plate and flask dose columns.
17.match_status: Whether the reported doses were equal or the microplate dose was the nearest available dose below or above the flask dose.
17.comparison_context_n: Number of attempted pairings of a microplate formulation and starting batch with a flask cohort at the listed doses. A cohort can occur in several pairings.
17.defined_context_n: Number of attempted pairings with a finite log₂ ratio for the specified quantity, requiring positive, available quantities in both formats.
17.plate_batch_n: Number of distinct microplate starting batches represented in pairings with a defined ratio.
17.flask_batch_n: Number of distinct shake-flask starting batches represented in pairings with a defined ratio.
17.plate_vessel_n: Number of distinct physical microplates recorded in pairings with a defined ratio, counting each plate identifier once.
17.flask_vessel_n: Number of distinct physical shake flasks recorded in pairings with a defined ratio, counting each flask identifier once.
17.median_log2_fold: Median across defined pairings of log₂(plate quantity/flask quantity). Zero denotes equality and +1 denotes a twofold larger plate quantity.
17.q25_log2_fold: 25th percentile of the defined log₂ plate/flask ratios across pairings.
17.q75_log2_fold: 75th percentile of the defined log₂ plate/flask ratios across pairings.
17.median_fold: Median log₂ ratio converted to the fold scale as 2 raised to that median. A value of 1 denotes equality between formats.
17.minimum_log2_fold: Smallest defined log₂ plate/flask ratio among the pairings.
17.maximum_log2_fold: Largest defined log₂ plate/flask ratio among the pairings.
17.final_read_maximum_context_n: Number of defined pairings in which at least one treated plate or flask trajectory reached its first observed maximum at the final acquisition.
17.status: Indicates a descriptive comparison across shared cohorts and controls, or an unavailable ratio because a quantity was missing or nonpositive.

18.LF_plate_context: Treatment of the Leptospirillum ferriphilum (LF) microplates. HH identifies medium without an added compound. Ga and In identify the gallium and indium sulfate treatments.
18.LF_Ga_mM: Ga concentration in the LF microplate treatment, in mM on a Ga cation basis.
18.LF_In_mM: In concentration in the LF microplate treatment, in mM on an In cation basis.
18.LF_batch_n: Number of distinct LF starting batches represented by eligible microplate endpoints.
18.LF_plate_n: Number of LF microplates with both a biotic and a matched abiotic change in absorbance at 380 nm (A380) at the final scheduled acquisition.
18.LF_inoculum_culture_n: Number of distinct inoculum cultures represented on the eligible LF microplates.
18.LF_biotic_mean_AU: Mean endpoint-minus-initial A380 of the inoculated LF wells, averaged within each eligible microplate and then across microplates, in absorbance units (AU).
18.LF_abiotic_mean_AU: Mean endpoint-minus-initial A380 of the matched uninoculated wells, averaged within each eligible LF microplate and then across microplates, in AU.
18.LF_net_change_AU: Mean across LF microplates of biotic minus matched abiotic change in A380, in AU.
18.LF_net_between_microplate_sd_AU: Sample standard deviation of the individual LF microplates’ biotic-minus-abiotic changes in A380, in AU.
18.LF_endpoint_min_d: Earliest final acquisition among the eligible LF microplates in this treatment, in days from the initial acquisition.
18.LF_endpoint_max_d: Latest final acquisition among the eligible LF microplates in this treatment, in days from the initial acquisition.
18.AF_reference_day_d: Time in days at which the Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans (AF) reference was evaluated, set to the latest LF acquisition across treatments.
18.AF_reference_mean_AU: Mean biotic change in A380 for no-additive AF controls, in AU. Each plate is evaluated at the reference day using an exact reading or interpolation between adjacent readings, then plates are averaged within batch and batch means receive equal weight.
18.AF_reference_batch_sd_AU: Sample standard deviation of the AF batch means at the reference day, in AU.
18.AF_batch_n: Number of AF starting batches contributing at least one eligible microplate to the reference.
18.AF_plate_n: Total number of AF control microplates with an eligible A380 estimate at the reference day.
18.LF_biotic_minus_AF_reference_AU: LF mean biotic change at its endpoint minus the time-matched AF reference mean, in AU, using biotic changes before abiotic subtraction.
18.status: Indicates that the comparison is descriptive because the LF treatment and AF reference differ in species, cohort, and medium.

19.cohort: Identifies either the fresh-starter L. ferriphilum experiment in HH medium at 37 °C or the tetrathionate tube experiment at 30 °C.
19.organism: Inoculated organism compared with matched abiotic tubes. LF denotes Leptospirillum ferriphilum, AF denotes Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans, and AT denotes Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans.
19.Ga_mM: Nominal Ga concentration in the biotic and matched abiotic tube treatment, in mM on a Ga cation basis.
19.In_mM: Nominal In concentration in the biotic and matched abiotic tube treatment, in mM on an In cation basis.
19.metric: Identifies the final measurement as oxidation–reduction potential versus Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl), measured pH, or fluorescence-derived apparent optical density at 600 nm using the AF calibration.
19.unit: Unit for the endpoint means, standard deviations, and difference, given as mV for oxidation–reduction potential, pH units for pH, or absorbance units (AU) for apparent OD600.
19.endpoint_d: Mean elapsed time in days of the inoculated tubes at their recorded final sampling event.
19.independent_batch_n: Number of distinct experimental batches represented by the inoculated tubes in this comparison.
19.biotic_starter_n: Number of distinct inoculum cultures used for the inoculated tubes in this comparison.
19.biotic_n: Number of distinct inoculated tubes with an eligible final measurement for the indicated metric.
19.abiotic_n: Number of distinct uninoculated tubes with an eligible final measurement in the matched batch, medium, treatment, temperature, and sampling event.
19.biotic_mean: Arithmetic mean of the eligible inoculated-tube endpoint measurements in the stated unit.
19.biotic_sd: Sample standard deviation among the eligible inoculated-tube endpoint measurements in the stated unit.
19.abiotic_mean: Arithmetic mean of the eligible matched abiotic-tube endpoint measurements in the stated unit.
19.abiotic_sd: Sample standard deviation among the eligible matched abiotic-tube endpoint measurements in the stated unit.
19.biotic_minus_abiotic: Mean inoculated-tube endpoint minus the matched abiotic-tube mean in the stated unit. A positive value indicates a higher final measurement in the inoculated tubes.
19.status: Identifies descriptive endpoint comparisons from one starting cohort with a shared starting-medium reference.

20.cohort: Baseline no-addition group defined by sulfur substrate and organism (AF for Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans or AT for Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans), with nominal substrate concentration or initial OD600 as indicated.
20.readout: Identifies the measured thymol-blue ratio R = A545/A485 or its scatter-corrected counterpart R* = (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750), where the numbers denote absorbance wavelengths in nm.
20.candidate_plate_n: Number of physical microplates scheduled for endpoint assessment in this cohort and readout before requiring both biotic and abiotic values.
20.paired_endpoint_plate_n: Number of microplates with finite biotic and matched abiotic changes for this readout at the final scheduled acquisition.
20.batch_n: Number of distinct batches represented by the microplates with paired biotic and abiotic endpoint changes.
20.inoculum_culture_n: Number of distinct inoculum cultures represented by the microplates with paired endpoint changes.
20.net_endpoint_change: Mean across eligible microplates of the biotic endpoint-minus-initial ratio change minus the corresponding abiotic change, in dimensionless ratio units.
20.net_between_microplate_sd: Sample standard deviation of net endpoint ratio changes across eligible microplates.
20.minimum_net_change: Smallest net endpoint ratio change observed among eligible microplates, in ratio units.
20.maximum_net_change: Largest net endpoint ratio change observed among eligible microplates, in ratio units.
20.endpoint_min_d: Earliest final scheduled acquisition among the eligible microplates, in days from the initial acquisition.
20.endpoint_max_d: Latest final scheduled acquisition among the eligible microplates, in days from the initial acquisition.
20.marginal_eligible_endpoint_plate_n: Number of microplates eligible for this readout’s biotic–abiotic endpoint contrast regardless of eligibility for the other readout.
20.common_eligible_endpoint_plate_n: Number of microplates eligible for both measured and corrected biotic–abiotic endpoint contrasts at the same scheduled acquisition.
20.status: Identifies a descriptive comparison among independent microplates from a single acquisition-date group.

21.species: Inoculated organism, identified as AF for Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans or AT for Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans.
21.medium: Medium formulation identifier used to group microplate treatments for the species.
21.candidate_plate_formulation_pairs: Number of physical microplate–formulation combinations considered for pairing measured and scatter-corrected endpoint ratios. A plate can contain several formulations.
21.paired_n: Number of microplate–formulation combinations with finite signed and magnitude scores for both readouts at the final scheduled acquisition, using the same eligible wells.
21.unavailable_pair_n: Number of candidate microplate–formulation combinations that lack a complete pair of endpoint scores.
21.batch_n: Number of distinct experimental batches represented by the complete pairs.
21.inoculum_culture_n: Number of distinct inoculum cultures represented by the complete pairs.
21.median_signed_snr_change: Median corrected-minus-measured change in dimensionless signed technical signal-to-noise score across paired microplate formulations. Each well’s net biotic-minus-abiotic ratio change is divided by the square root of the sum of the initial and endpoint abiotic variances, then signed scores are averaged within each plate formulation.
21.signed_snr_q25: 25th percentile of the paired corrected-minus-measured differences in signed signal-to-noise score.
21.signed_snr_q75: 75th percentile of the paired corrected-minus-measured differences in signed signal-to-noise score.
21.median_magnitude_change: Median corrected-minus-measured change in score magnitude across paired microplate formulations. For each readout, absolute well-level scores are averaged within the plate formulation before taking the difference.
21.magnitude_q25: 25th percentile of the paired corrected-minus-measured differences in mean absolute signal-to-noise score.
21.magnitude_q75: 75th percentile of the paired corrected-minus-measured differences in mean absolute signal-to-noise score.
21.magnitude_increased_n: Number of complete pairs for which correction strictly increased the mean absolute score.
21.magnitude_increased_percent: Percentage of all complete pairs for which correction strictly increased the mean absolute score.
21.direction_agreement_percent: Percentage of complete pairs in which the measured and corrected signed plate scores have the same sign, counting two zero scores as agreement.
21.status: Identifies descriptive paired comparisons across formulations, some of which share the same physical microplate.

22.species: Inoculated organism, identified as AF for Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans or LF for Leptospirillum ferriphilum.
22.stratum: Grouping of plate conditions by added-compound class or absence of additions. The no-addition group includes the recorded preparation and pH settings.
22.candidate_plate_condition_n: Number of distinct physical microplate–condition combinations considered for screening, counting each plate and treatment column once across recorded acquisitions.
22.physical_plate_n: Number of distinct physical microplates contributing candidate conditions to this group.
22.starter_batch_n: Number of distinct starting batches represented by the candidate plate conditions.
22.evaluable_decision_n: Number of plate conditions with either an observed event or a complete paired record establishing no event.
22.unevaluable_decision_n: Number of candidate plate conditions with no observed event and too little paired biotic and abiotic coverage to classify them as negative.
22.event_n: Number of plate conditions with at least one postbaseline acquisition at which mean biotic A380 rose by at least 1 AU and matched abiotic A380 rose by less than 1 AU from their respective initial readings.
22.event_percent: Percentage of evaluable plate conditions that met the event criterion at least once.
22.no_event_n: Number of plate conditions with no event, a finite initial pair, and finite biotic and abiotic values at every recorded postbaseline acquisition, including at least one such acquisition.
22.partial_no_event_n: Number of unevaluable plate conditions with no observed event and at least one finite postbaseline biotic–abiotic pair, but incomplete coverage of the initial or postbaseline pairs.
22.first_event_net_min_AU: Smallest net change in A380 at the first qualifying acquisition across event-positive plate conditions, in AU. Net change is the biotic change from baseline minus the matched abiotic change.
22.first_event_net_q25_AU: 25th percentile of net A380 changes at the first qualifying acquisition for each event-positive plate condition, in AU.
22.first_event_net_median_AU: Median net A380 change at the first qualifying acquisition for each event-positive plate condition, in AU.
22.first_event_net_q75_AU: 75th percentile of net A380 changes at the first qualifying acquisition for each event-positive plate condition, in AU.
22.event_without_net_1AU_n: Number of event-positive plate conditions whose net biotic-minus-abiotic A380 change remained below 1 AU at every qualifying acquisition.
22.event_without_net_1AU_percent: Percentage of event-positive plate conditions whose net A380 change remained below 1 AU at every qualifying acquisition.
22.observed_window_median_d: Median elapsed time to the last recorded postbaseline acquisition across candidate plate conditions with a recorded duration, in days.
22.status: Identifies descriptive classifications of the recorded optical screen for apparent iron oxidation.

23.species: Inoculated organism, identified as AF for Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans or LF for Leptospirillum ferriphilum.
23.stratum: Group of conditions defined by the added-compound class or absence of additions.
23.comparison_level: Within a starting batch, compares binary outcomes across plates at the same condition. Between batches, compares the fractions of plates that passed at that condition. A plate passes when a postbaseline biotic A380 increase of at least 1 AU coincides with a matched abiotic increase below 1 AU.
23.candidate_comparison_n: Number of repeated groups at the indicated level, counting condition–batch groups with at least two physical plates or conditions represented by at least two batches.
23.evaluable_comparison_n: Number of candidate groups for which every contributing plate could be classified as event-positive or a complete no-event observation.
23.incomplete_comparison_n: Number of candidate groups containing at least one unevaluable plate decision.
23.identical_event_fraction_n: Number of evaluable groups with identical outcomes across plates within batch or identical positive-plate fractions across batches.
23.identical_event_fraction_percent: Percentage of evaluable groups with a zero range in plate outcomes or batch positive-plate fractions.
23.event_fraction_range_median_pp: Median group range among evaluable comparisons, in percentage points. Within a batch the range is 0 or 100 points across plate outcomes. Between batches it is the highest minus the lowest percentage of plates passing.
23.event_fraction_range_q25_pp: 25th percentile of the group ranges in event frequency across evaluable comparisons, in percentage points.
23.event_fraction_range_q75_pp: 75th percentile of the group ranges in event frequency across evaluable comparisons, in percentage points.
23.event_fraction_range_max_pp: Largest group range in event frequency among evaluable comparisons, in percentage points.
23.all_positive_comparison_n: Number of evaluable groups in which every constituent plate screened positive.
23.all_negative_comparison_n: Number of evaluable groups in which every constituent plate had a complete no-event result.
23.identical_mixed_comparison_n: Number of between-batch comparisons in which every batch had the same positive-plate fraction strictly between zero and one.
23.discordant_comparison_n: Number of evaluable groups in which plate outcomes within a batch or positive-plate fractions between batches differed.
23.disagreement_percent: Percentage of evaluable groups with a nonzero range in plate outcomes or batch positive-plate fractions.
23.status: Indicates whether repeated groups supported a descriptive consistency estimate or no repeated group was evaluable.

24.acid_M: Nominal sulfuric acid concentration (M) in the ferric standards used for this acid-specific calibration.
24.validation: Identifies whether cross-validation withheld one physical microplate at a time or withheld one of the ten interior dilution levels across all microplates at once.
24.nominal_reference_window_mM: Nominal total-iron concentration window (mM) defined by dilution rank. “all” includes all attempted levels in the indicated scheme.
24.reference_min_mM: Lowest measured total-iron reference concentration (mM) among the attempted predictions in this row.
24.reference_max_mM: Highest measured total-iron reference concentration (mM) among the attempted predictions in this row.
24.plate_n: Number of distinct physical microplates represented among the withheld observations in this row.
24.attempted_n: Number of withheld plate-by-standard mean absorbances for which a total-iron concentration prediction was attempted.
24.predicted_n: Number of attempts yielding a finite concentration prediction within the acid-specific training range.
24.failed_n: Number of attempts for which an eligible concentration prediction was unavailable.
24.outside_reference_support_n: Number of attempts whose measured total-iron reference lay outside the concentration range used to fit the model for that acid.
24.response_or_inverse_failure_n: Number of attempts with a reference inside the training range but no valid inverse prediction, including missing responses, fit failures, and responses outside the fitted response range.
24.converged_unidentified_fit_n: Number of withheld observations whose training fit converged but failed the model’s parameter-identification checks. An observation may still yield a prediction.
24.bias_mM: Mean signed concentration error (predicted minus measured total Fe, mM) over successful predictions.
24.rmse_mM: Root mean squared concentration error (mM) over successful predictions.
24.median_absolute_error_mM: Median absolute difference between predicted and measured total-iron concentration (mM) over successful predictions.
24.median_absolute_relative_error_percent: Median absolute concentration error divided by the measured concentration and expressed as a percentage, using successful predictions with a positive reference.
24.relative_error_n: Number of successful predictions with a positive measured reference, the denominator for the relative-error summary.
24.plate_rmse_min_mM: Smallest plate-specific root mean squared concentration error (mM) among plates with at least one successful prediction.
24.plate_rmse_max_mM: Largest plate-specific root mean squared concentration error (mM) among plates with at least one successful prediction.

25.acid_M: Nominal sulfuric acid concentration (M) of the withheld ferric standards being evaluated.
25.validation: Identifies whether cross-validation withheld one physical microplate at a time or withheld one interior dilution level across all microplates at once.
25.plate_n: Number of distinct physical microplates represented among the withheld observations at this acid concentration.
25.attempted_n: Number of distinct withheld plate-by-standard mean absorbances submitted to both models.
25.paired_prediction_n: Number of withheld observations with finite absorbance predictions from both models within the acid-specific training concentration range. Both error summaries use these same observations.
25.shared_rmse_AU: Root mean squared error of predicted 380 nm absorbance (AU) for a single calibration curve fitted across all acid concentrations.
25.shared_bias_AU: Mean signed error in 380 nm absorbance (predicted minus measured, AU) for the shared calibration curve.
25.acid_specific_rmse_AU: Root mean squared error of predicted 380 nm absorbance (AU) for the curve fitted only to training standards at the indicated acid concentration.
25.acid_specific_bias_AU: Mean signed error in 380 nm absorbance (predicted minus measured, AU) for the acid-specific curve.
25.rmse_change_AU: Acid-specific RMSE minus shared-model RMSE (AU). Negative values indicate lower error for the acid-specific model.
25.squared_error_reduction_percent: Percentage reduction in mean squared error relative to the shared model, calculated as 100 × [1 − (acid-specific RMSE / shared RMSE)²]. Negative values indicate larger acid-specific error.

26.family: Identifies initial indicator calibration in chemical standards or indicator validation in growth media.
26.cohort: Calibration condition (sulfuric acid or thymol blue concentration) or growth medium used for this interval.
26.readout: Indicator response used for the two standards. R and R* are the measured and scatter-corrected pH ratios, and A380 and A*380 are the measured and scatter-corrected 380 nm absorbances.
26.assay: Identifies whether pH or iron concentration defines the standards.
26.reference_unit: Unit of the reference values and the denominator of the secant slope. The scale is pH for pH standards, measured total Fe (mM) for initial iron calibration, or added Fe (mM) for iron in growth media.
26.interval_rank: Position of the adjacent pair in increasing reference order within a plate, starting at 0 for the first pair.
26.scheduled_plate_n: Number of physical microplates scheduled for this adjacent reference interval, including plates with an unavailable response.
26.reference_low: Mean lower endpoint of the reference interval across the scheduled plates, in the stated reference unit.
26.reference_high: Mean upper endpoint of the reference interval across the scheduled plates, in the stated reference unit.
26.response_change_n: Number of physical plates with a finite response change for this interval.
26.response_change: Mean across plates of the higher-reference standard’s mean response minus the lower-reference standard’s mean response, in ratio units for pH or AU for iron.
26.response_change_ci_low: Lower limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean signed response change.
26.response_change_ci_high: Upper limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean signed response change.
26.secant_sensitivity_n: Number of physical plates with a finite slope between these adjacent reference levels.
26.secant_sensitivity: Mean across plates of the signed response change divided by the reference interval width on that plate, in response units per reference unit.
26.secant_sensitivity_ci_low: Lower limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean slope between adjacent standards.
26.secant_sensitivity_ci_high: Upper limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean slope between adjacent standards.
26.change_over_noise_n: Number of physical plates with a positive, finite ratio of absolute response change to combined technical-well SD.
26.change_over_noise: Geometric mean across plates of the absolute response change divided by √(SD_low² + SD_high²), using the within-standard well SD at each endpoint. This ratio is dimensionless.
26.change_over_noise_ci_low: Lower limit of the pointwise 95% confidence interval for the geometric mean change-to-noise ratio, calculated on the log scale with Student’s t and transformed back.
26.change_over_noise_ci_high: Upper limit of the pointwise 95% confidence interval for the geometric mean change-to-noise ratio, calculated on the log scale with Student’s t and transformed back.
26.opposite_direction_plate_n: Number of plates on which the pH-indicator response increased as pH increased or iron absorbance decreased as iron concentration increased.
26.interval_status: Indicates whether the signed response change was estimated from at least two physical plates, observed on a single plate, or unavailable.

27.assay: Identifies whether the handling comparison used the pH indicator or the ferric iron absorbance indicator.
27.readout: Measured or scatter-corrected pH ratio (R or R*) or 380 nm absorbance (A380 or A*380) used for the comparison.
27.dye: Nominal thymol blue concentration in the standards (µM).
27.material: Microplate material for the candidate acquisition, identified as UV-transparent or non-UV-transparent.
27.contrast: Pair of handling conditions being compared. The candidate appears first and its reference second, including the two acquisitions used for membrane and lid comparisons.
27.step_id: Identifier of the candidate incubation or acquisition step. The lid-present/lid-absent comparison has no separate incubation-step identifier.
27.acid_M: Nominal sulfuric acid concentration (M) where a single acid background defines the calibration series.
27.paired_plate_n: Total number of paired candidate and reference microplate comparisons in this row, including pairs lacking an estimate for a particular metric.
27.span_plate_n: Number of plate pairs with positive finite response spans for both conditions.
27.span_fold_estimate: Geometric mean of candidate/reference response-span ratios across eligible plate pairs. Each span is the maximum minus minimum mean response among common complete standard levels.
27.span_fold_ci_low: Lower limit of the 95% confidence interval for the span fold, obtained from a Student’s t interval on the plate-pair log₂ ratios and transformed back.
27.span_fold_ci_high: Upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the span fold, obtained from a Student’s t interval on the plate-pair log₂ ratios and transformed back.
27.sd_plate_n: Number of plate pairs with positive finite pooled within-standard SDs for both conditions.
27.sd_fold_estimate: Geometric mean of candidate/reference technical SD ratios across eligible plate pairs. Each technical SD pools well variances across common complete standard levels, weighted by their degrees of freedom.
27.sd_fold_ci_low: Lower limit of the 95% confidence interval for the technical SD fold, obtained from a Student’s t interval on the plate-pair log₂ ratios and transformed back.
27.sd_fold_ci_high: Upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the technical SD fold, obtained from a Student’s t interval on the plate-pair log₂ ratios and transformed back.
27.local_plate_n: Number of plate pairs with an estimable local separation score in both handling conditions.
27.local_estimate: Mean paired difference in local separation (candidate minus reference). For each plate, divide each eligible adjacent change by √[(SD_low² + SD_high²)/2], assign positive scores to decreasing pH signal or increasing iron signal as the reference increases, then take the median score.
27.local_ci_low: Lower limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plate pairs for the mean difference in local separation.
27.local_ci_high: Upper limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plate pairs for the mean difference in local separation.
27.reference_reversal_plate_n: Number of plate pairs in which the reference condition had at least one eligible adjacent interval with a response change opposite to the expected direction.
27.candidate_reversal_plate_n: Number of plate pairs in which the candidate condition had at least one eligible adjacent interval with a response change opposite to the expected direction.
27.span_status: Whether the span fold was estimated from multiple plate pairs, available for one pair without a confidence interval, or unavailable.
27.sd_status: Whether the technical SD fold was estimated from multiple plate pairs, available for one pair without a confidence interval, or unavailable.
27.local_status: Whether the local separation difference was estimated from multiple plate pairs, available for one pair without a confidence interval, or unavailable.

28.cohort: Identifies whether the ratio eligibility counts describe optical standards or sulfur microplate cultures.
28.experiment_id: Experimental series identifier linking the acquired well measurements to the deposit’s experimental records.
28.plate_type: UV-transparent or non-UV-transparent plate designation for optical standards. This field is blank for the sulfur culture rows.
28.medium_id: Medium identifier when an optical standard series is subdivided by growth medium.
28.plate_n: Number of distinct physical microplates contributing acquired well measurements to this row.
28.attempt_n: Total acquired well measurements across those plates, counting each well once per acquisition even when neither ratio was eligible.
28.raw_valid_n: Number of acquired well measurements yielding an eligible measured ratio, R = A545/A485.
28.corrected_valid_n: Number of acquired well measurements yielding an eligible corrected ratio, R* = (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750).
28.both_valid_n: Number of acquired well measurements for which both the measured and scatter-corrected ratios were eligible.
28.raw_only_n: Number of acquired well measurements for which only the measured ratio was eligible.
28.corrected_only_n: Number of acquired well measurements for which only the scatter-corrected ratio was eligible.
28.neither_valid_n: Number of acquired well measurements for which neither ratio was eligible.
28.raw_percent_mean: Mean across plates of the percentage of each plate’s acquired well measurements yielding an eligible measured ratio, with equal weight per plate.
28.corrected_percent_mean: Mean across plates of the percentage of each plate’s acquired well measurements yielding an eligible corrected ratio, with equal weight per plate.
28.difference_pp_mean: Mean of the plate-specific differences in eligible percentages (corrected minus measured), in percentage points.
28.difference_pp_min: Smallest plate-specific difference in eligible percentages (corrected minus measured), in percentage points.
28.difference_pp_max: Largest plate-specific difference in eligible percentages (corrected minus measured), in percentage points.
28.culture_type: Biotic or abiotic well designation for the sulfur microplate cultures. This field is blank for optical standards.

29.plate_dose: Microplate formulation, listing each added component and its concentration in mM. Metal salts are expressed on a cation basis.
29.flask_dose: Shake-flask formulation, listing each added component and its nominal concentration in mM on the same chemical basis as the plate.
29.dose_match: Whether the reported concentrations are equal or the microplate dose is the closest available dose below or above the flask dose. Multicomponent formulations require equality for every component.
29.candidate_context_n: Number of distinct comparisons between a flask condition and a set of physical plates in a plate batch at this dose pair, before checking trajectory support.
29.paired_context_n: Number of candidate comparisons with calculable errors for both plate readouts over the same overlap with the flask trajectory.
29.unavailable_context_n: Number of candidate comparisons lacking a valid trajectory error for one or both plate readouts.
29.cohort_pair_n: Number of distinct flask-condition and plate-batch combinations contributing to the mean errors. Multiple eligible comparisons within a combination are averaged first.
29.plate_batch_n: Number of distinct microplate batches represented among all candidate comparisons for this dose pair.
29.flask_batch_n: Number of distinct shake-flask batches represented among all candidate comparisons for this dose pair.
29.raw_error: Time-weighted mean absolute difference between the net measured A380 trajectory and the flask Fe(II)-depletion trajectory. Each curve is centered at the overlap start and divided by its own positive change over the overlap. The dimensionless errors are averaged equally across cohort pairs.
29.corrected_error: The same dimensionless, time-weighted mean absolute difference using net scatter-corrected A380 (A380 − A750) and the same flask trajectory, averaged equally across the same cohort pairs.
29.paired_error_difference: Mean corrected error minus measured error across matched cohort pairs. A negative value means closer agreement in trajectory shape after correction.
29.error_improved_context_percent: Percentage of eligible paired comparisons in which corrected error is strictly lower than measured error, counting each comparison once.
29.window_min_d: Earliest ending day of the shared plate–flask observation window among candidate comparisons, measured from incubation start.
29.window_max_d: Latest ending day of the shared plate–flask observation window among candidate comparisons, measured from incubation start.
29.status: Identifies a descriptive trajectory comparison using reused cohorts, for which no equivalence test was performed.

30.additive: Treatment component whose concentration varies. Metal symbols denote the cation supplied by its salt.
30.plate_dose_mM: Reported microplate concentration of the variable additive in mM, expressed on a cation basis for metal salts.
30.flask_dose_mM: Nominal shake-flask concentration of the variable additive in mM, on the same chemical basis as the plate dose.
30.Ga_mM: Additional Ga(III) concentration in mM for the citric acid series. For the gallium dose series itself, the doses appear in the plate and flask dose columns.
30.match_status: Whether the reported doses are equal or the microplate dose is the nearest available dose below or above the flask dose.
30.candidate_context_n: Number of distinct plate-batch and flask-condition comparisons identified for this formulation and dose pair before window eligibility is checked.
30.paired_context_n: Number of comparisons in which both formats had an eligible primary response and all primary-eligible vessels also had a calculable common-window response.
30.unavailable_context_n: Number of candidate comparisons lacking complete paired primary and common-window estimates in both formats.
30.plate_batch_n: Number of distinct microplate batches in all candidate comparisons for the dose pair.
30.flask_batch_n: Number of distinct shake-flask batches in all candidate comparisons for the dose pair.
30.plate_response_change_pp: Mean change in microplate control-relative AUC, in percentage points, using the shared window instead of integrating each trajectory to its own first maximum. Response is 100 times treated AUC divided by mean control AUC. Vessel results are averaged within comparisons before averaging across comparisons.
30.flask_response_change_pp: Corresponding mean change in flask control-relative AUC, in percentage points, calculated as shared-window response minus response to each trajectory’s first maximum.
30.format_difference_change_pp: Change in the plate-minus-flask response difference, in percentage points, calculated as the shared-window difference minus the primary difference.
30.primary_format_difference_pp: Mean microplate response minus flask response, in percentage points, when each treatment and control trajectory is integrated to its own first observed maximum.
30.fixed_format_difference_pp: Mean microplate response minus flask response, in percentage points, when all treatment and control trajectories in a comparison are integrated over their shared observation window.
30.window_min_d: Earliest available common ending day among candidate comparisons. Each comparison ends at the earliest final reading of its plate, flask, and assigned control trajectories.
30.window_max_d: Latest available common ending day among candidate comparisons, in days from incubation start.
30.status: Identifies a descriptive window-sensitivity comparison with shared controls and cohorts. No population-level test was performed.

31.readout: Identifies apparent flask Fe(III) generation from Fe(II) depletion (mM), net biotic-minus-abiotic change in plate A380 (AU), or abiotic change in plate A380 (AU).
31.citric_acid_mM: Citric acid concentration in the treated condition, in mM.
31.reference_citric_acid_mM: Citric acid concentration of the matched reference, 0 mM for every contrast.
31.Ga_mM: Ga(III) concentration in mM, held equal in the treated condition and its zero-citric-acid reference.
31.candidate_batch_n: Number of experimental batches containing a treated vessel for this readout, citric acid concentration, and gallium concentration.
31.paired_batch_n: Number of batches with at least one eligible treated–reference endpoint pair.
31.candidate_unit_n: Number of treated physical microplates or shake flasks considered for the endpoint comparison.
31.paired_unit_n: Number of treated units with a finite matched reference at the same final acquisition and elapsed time. Plate conditions are paired within physical plate and flask cultures by batch and starter culture.
31.unavailable_unit_n: Number of candidate treated units lacking an eligible pair because the reference, final acquisition, timing, or measured endpoint could not be matched.
31.mean_effect: Mean treated endpoint minus matched zero-citric-acid endpoint, in the units of the readout. Pair differences are averaged within batches, then batch means receive equal weight.
31.between_batch_effect_sd: Sample SD of the batch mean endpoint differences, in the units of the readout, for two or more eligible batches.
31.within_batch_pair_sd: Sample SD among unit-pair endpoint differences, in the units of the readout, when a single batch contributes at least two eligible pairs.
31.ci_low: Lower limit of the two-sided 95% Student’s t interval for the mean endpoint effect, calculated from two or more independent batch means.
31.ci_high: Upper limit of the same two-sided 95% Student’s t interval, in AU for plate readouts or mM for flasks.
31.endpoint_min_d: Earliest elapsed day of a matched final acquisition among eligible treated–reference pairs.
31.endpoint_max_d: Latest elapsed day of a matched final acquisition among eligible treated–reference pairs.
31.status: Indicates whether a batch-based confidence interval was estimable, only one eligible batch contributed a descriptive mean, or no eligible endpoint pair was available.

32.experiment_id: Identifier linking the sulfur-culture experiment to the microplate records and experimental metadata.
32.cohort: Short label for the organism, medium, treatment series, and starting inoculum OD600 encoded by the experiment identifier.
32.plate_n: Number of physical microplates summarized for the experiment.
32.postinitial_condition_acquisition_n: Total number of postinitial condition measurements across plates, counting each treatment condition on each plate at each acquisition once.
32.common_valid_n: Number of postinitial condition measurements valid for both ratios on the same three biotic wells, with eligible baselines and complete matched abiotic controls.
32.nonzero_common_n: Number of jointly valid comparisons in which the mean net change was nonzero for both measured and scatter-corrected ratios. Net change is biotic change from baseline minus the matched abiotic change.
32.opposite_sign_n: Total number of jointly valid, nonzero comparisons in which the two within-plate mean net changes had opposite signs.
32.opposite_sign_percent: Mean of the within-plate percentages of jointly valid, nonzero comparisons with opposite signs. Each plate with an eligible denominator receives equal weight.
32.opposite_sign_percent_min: Lowest observed opposite-sign percentage among physical plates with a jointly valid, nonzero comparison.
32.opposite_sign_percent_max: Highest observed opposite-sign percentage among physical plates with a jointly valid, nonzero comparison.
32.raw_comparison_yield_percent: Mean percentage of all postinitial condition measurements on each plate with an eligible net change for the measured ratio A545/A485, weighting physical plates equally.
32.corrected_comparison_yield_percent: Mean percentage of all postinitial condition measurements on each plate with an eligible net change for the corrected ratio (A545 − A750)/(A485 − A750), weighting physical plates equally.
